significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that non-dominant-language reasoning passes through a dominant-language representation that is "causally load-bearing," with "reliance on this pivot" increasing with typological or resource distance. This combines a form-(ii) causal mechanism with a form-(iii) ordering and predictive coupling: language distance would predict pivot alignment, ablation sensitivity, and cross-lingual accuracy gaps, while the lexical-versus-abstract distinction would constrain whether the mechanism is translation or shared-concept computation. It establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism; a verified-false result would rule out this specific load-bearing interlingua account, although failure of only the distance relation would not rule out pivoting itself, so the compound hypothesis is somewhat less determinate than a single law. Wendler et al. (ACL 2024) made intermediate English-leaning representations relevant to latent-language explanations, but the topic-substitution check lowers the assessment from the highest bands: multilingual shared-versus-language-specific mechanisms alone would not earn this score, whereas the claim-specific causal bottleneck and distance-dependent law do.

reach.justification: The claim names three usable handles: a "layerwise pivot-alignment score," the "dominant-language pivot direction" as an ablation or steering target, and the proposed relation between "baseline pivot reliance and cross-lingual accuracy gap." The alignment score is mainly a post-hoc diagnostic, but the predictive coupling can provide limited ex-ante lead time by flagging languages likely to exhibit reasoning gaps before deployment, while "pivot-agnostic fine-tuning" supplies a design direction rather than a fully specified intervention. After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion would still predict greater reliance and ablation damage for distant or low-resource languages, so a relation—not merely a search procedure—could transfer across dominant-language-centric multilingual models, with model auditors and trainers as plausible downstream users; the claim does not support broad uptake outside AI and explicitly allows balanced models to differ. The topic-substitution check passes: the general topic would not itself provide any diagnostic or predictor, while these claim-specific handles justify reach above the topic median.
